what_it_does: Machine-learning models for chip design automation (EDA) need large circuit datasets to train effectively, but companies cannot share proprietary circuit designs due to intellectual-property concerns. FedEDA enables federated learning — each company trains a local model on private data and shares only the learned weights, not raw circuits. The algorithm uses Rent's Rule (a principle that relates circuit size to wiring) to align models across companies with different data distributions, improving weight aggregation quality and enabling collaborative model training without exposing secrets.
